title: Personal Credit Cards: points needed to cover what the card owes when it is paid down with points
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: the amount owed that a points statement credit pays

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When a cardholder uses rewards points to pay down what a card owes, it fixes the amount the points are to pay and the number of points that cover it.

## Entry condition

Every late payment fee on the card that was billed contrary to the charter has been reversed before the rewards statement credit is sized. The purpose is that the amount the points pay reflects only what the cardholder owes. Where that condition is unmet, the statement credit is not sized.

## Rule

1. The amount to be paid is the card's current amount owed at handling time, after those reversals.
2. The points that cover it are that amount divided by the card tier's cash value per point, rounded up to the next whole point.
3. An amount owed of zero or below, that is a card in credit or at nil, needs no points.

## Effect of a reversal made first (hypothetical figures, value per point 0.03 USD)

A late payment fee of 30.00 USD that was billed contrary to the charter is reversed before sizing. The amount owed falls by 30.00 USD, so the points that cover it fall by 30.00 divided by 0.03, that is 1000 points.

## Worked examples (hypothetical value per point of 0.03 USD, not a tier value)

| Current amount owed at handling time | Quotient | Points that cover it |
|---|---|---|
| 215.37 USD | 7179 exactly | 7179 |
| 215.38 USD | 7179.33 | 7180 |
| 0.00 USD | not computed | 0 |
| minus 12.00 USD, a credit | not computed | 0 |

## Wrong reading and correct basis

- **Wrong:** size the points on the amount owed as it stood before a fee billed contrary to the charter was reversed. **Correct:** those fees are reversed first, and the amount owed after them is used.
- **Wrong:** round the quotient to the nearest point. **Correct:** round up to the next whole point; a whole quotient stays as it is.
